problem:
$$
f(t,z)=⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\text{_____},\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,z)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $9{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=36.$ What is the second component of $f?$
worked_solution:
Recall that the ellipse 

$$
9{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=36\,⟹\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{36}=1
$$

in $xy$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,y⟩=⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,6\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,t\in [0,2\pi ),
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{36} & =\frac{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(6\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}}{36} \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,6\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in [0,2\pi )$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $6\operatorname{sin}⁡t.$
